Subject: PoC decision & next steps — deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Olivia / Kevin —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC and scope (short version for your procurement & infra teams below).

Call recap (what I heard):
- Primary use case: transaction classification and enrichment for real-time analyst workflows (sensitive financial data).
- Non-negotiables: audit logs, strict access controls, and US-only data residency.
- Preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, but FinLytics is evaluating Private VPC if encryption/KMS requirements push that route. Hosted API is acceptable for an initial evaluation only if data can be masked and meets security checks.

Proposed PoC (3-week focused trial):
- Week 0 (kickoff): confirm deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Complete security questionnaire and share procurement contact.
- Week 1: Provision environment (Dedicated pool or Private VPC). Connect sample app and ingest a 50k-row anonymized dataset.
- Week 2: Run latency/throughput tests + integration checks (KV/prefix caching, batching).
- Week 3: Iterate on performance, produce runbook + cost model, decision milestone.

Success criteria (suggested):
- Production-like SLOs: median response time < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for 2k-token requests under the agreed workload profile.
- Throughput: sustain 150 reqs/min with <5% tail error rate.
- Security: audit logs enabled, KMS-backed encryption at rest, and evidence of SOC2 controls in place.
- Operational: documented rollback and failover paths; handoff materials for your infra team.

Proposed kickoff: next Wednesday (2025-11-12) morning PT. Please confirm stakeholders — I have Olivia and Kevin listed as product + infra; please add procurement contact (procurement@finlytics.com) and a technical owner for network/VPC setup.

Attachments: finlytics_poc_scope_v1.pdf (draft scope), redwood-deployment-options-onepager.pdf

If this matches your expectations, I will assemble the internal PoC runbook and schedule a 30-min kickoff with our SE (Priyom) and engineering on-call.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: PoC decision & next steps — deployment mode tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Great — appreciate the clarity. Below is a concrete PoC timeline and owner matrix so procurement has what they need for an estimate.

PoC timeline & deliverables (detailed):
- Day 0 (Kickoff): 30-min call to confirm scope, sign the short PoC agreement, and assign technical contacts. (Owners: Rishi / Olivia)
- Week 1 (Provisioning): Redwood provisions Dedicated pool (or Private VPC if you confirm KMS/HSM needs). SE tasks: network connectivity, test tokens, sample ingest. Deliverable: provisioned environment + connection guide. (Owners: Redwood SE - Priyom; FinLytics infra - Kevin)
- Week 2 (Validation): Run benchmark scenarios using your anonymized dataset. Validate latency SLOs and throughput; instrument tracing and costs per request. Deliverable: benchmark report + latency/throughput dashboard. (Owners: Redwood SE / FinLytics PM)
- Week 3 (Optimization & Handoff): Tune batching / caching, produce final cost model, runbook, and decision memo. (Owners: Redwood Eng / FinLytics stakeholders)

Success criteria (finalized):
- Functional: model outputs meet the quality gate for 95% of sampled prompts (we'll agree on the evaluation prompts during kickoff).
- Performance: median < 80ms, p95 < 200ms under the test traffic profile.
- Security & Compliance: audit logs, KMS encryption, and documented access controls.
- Budget: projected monthly cost for steady-state Dedicated must be within the estimate provided to procurement.

What we need from FinLytics before kickoff:
1) Confirm preferred deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
2) Provide procurement contact and required PO or contract template if you prefer.
3) Share anonymized sample dataset and an evaluation prompt set (can be synthetic but representative).
4) Identify a technical owner for network/VPC peering or service account/KMS access (Kevin, please confirm).

I'll attach the PoC scope doc and a short one-pager that captures deployment tradeoffs. If you give the thumbs up, Marissa will coordinate the contract / credit estimate for procurement.

Attachments: finlytics_poc_scope_v1.pdf, redwood-deployment-options-onepager.pdf

Thanks — I will schedule the kickoff for 11/12 and block a 30-min slot pending your confirmation.

Best,
Rishi

Subject: Internal: FinLytics PoC — SE checklist & blockers

Internal note — copying the SE checklist I'll include in the kickoff packet. Keeping this internal-only for now.

Quick technical checklist (Provisioning notes):
- Dedicated: reserve a 4x A10G-equivalent pool for the PoC to match expected concurrency (can scale down after). Configure continuous batching and enable prefix caching.
- Private VPC: requires cross-account VPC peering, route tables, and a customer-managed KMS key. Plan for ~3–5 business days for networking & KMS approvals.
- Hosted (evaluation): need to confirm that no PII will be sent; otherwise we require tokenization on the client side.

Potential blockers and mitigations:
- KMS/HSM access: if FinLytics requires HSM-backed keys, schedule early — this adds operational time.
- VPC peering & firewall rules: get Kevin to provide the CIDR ranges and appropriate IAM role in advance.
- Data volume: large datasets (>500k rows) will need a staged ingest approach.

Attachments (internal): deploy-prereqs-checklist.xlsx

Action items for our prep:
1) Prepare Dedicated cost estimate template for Marissa to send to procurement.
2) Draft a short security attestation that answers the most common procurement questions (SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, retention).
3) Ensure an SE is on-call during Week 2 benchmarks.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
